_provenance: Neural control of a fixed body, GPU-batched across 16 randomized start poses. The brain's ONLY job is to produce a coordinated gait — distance, periodicity (rhythm, not noise), and robustness (limit cycle, not lottery ticket). The body is fixed (walker.trained.json); the GAIT IS A LIMIT CYCLE, and nothing in the old brain.json ever rewarded rhythm, so the old champion was a convulsion with good PR.

walls.periodicity: The footfall signal MUST contain a cycle. Autocorrelation of the support signal: 1.0 is a metronome, 0.0 is a seizure. Below 0.35 means the creature scrabbles rather than strides. NOTHING in the old objective rewarded rhythm, so nothing ever stopped the brain from being a convulsion that happened to travel — and it scored 0.25, and we called it a bound. THIS IS A GAIT, NOT FALLING WITH STYLE.
walls.robustness: The worst of 16 randomized start poses MUST reach at least 75% of the mean distance. THE ANTI-LOTTERY. A real limit cycle converges onto the same gait from every start (~1.0); a chaotic fraud scores near 0. The old champion scored 0.686 — lower than untrained brains. This IS the measure the 16x eval cost was designed for.
walls.torso_z: The body MUST stand up. The baseline is 0.027 body lengths — the body is LYING DOWN, dragging itself with five bones in contact at all times. Below 0.08 means the creature is a worm, not an animal. This is a declared preference, not physics; a superior slither is physically real and this wall would block it honestly.
walls.sleds: No more than ONE bone MUST drag continuously. A link in contact >92% of the time is not a foot — it is a SLED. The baseline has five sleds; a hard gate would zero the starting population, so this is soft. But more than one sled means the creature is a tripod with a tail, not a walker.
walls.energy: Joint work MUST stay bounded. Above 900 J per meter means every actuator is fighting at full torque — the brain is not coordinating, it is seizing. The old winner measured 888; ref set AT the measurement so the gradient is maximum where the optimiser lives.
